newsitem.title: UK: British Midland gets good Denmark cargo yields.
newsitem.headline: British Midland gets good Denmark cargo yields.

text.p: London Heathrow-Copenhagen is proving to be the most successful in terms of cargo volumes and yields of British Midland's three new UK-Scandinavia routes, cargo manager Terry Greetham said.

On April 21, the carrier began daily return services from Heathrow to Copenhagen, Gothenburg and Oslo to add to existing other Scandinavian flights from Heathrow to Bergen and Glasgow/Edinburgh-Copenhagen.

"Cargo prospects for the new Copenhagen route in particular look very promising. Denmark is an important trading partner of Britain's and I think we will do well, despite competition from British Airways, SAS and truckers," said Greetham.

After Copenhagen, he listed Gothenburg, Oslo and Bergen is order of importance as cargo routes for British Midland, which is 40 percent owned by SAS. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
